Incumbent Republican senator [[Lisa Murkowski]] won reelection to a fourth full term, defeating fellow Republican Kelly Tshibaka and [[Democratic Party (United States)|Democrat]] Patricia Chesbro.Gomez, Henry J. "[https://www.nbcnews.com/politics/2022-election/sen-lisa-murkowski-wins-re-election-alaska-fending-trump-backed-challe-rcna58447 Sen. Lisa Murkowski wins re-election in Alaska, fending off Trump-backed challenge after a ranked-choice runoff]", [[NBC News]] (November 23, 2022). This was the first U.S. Senate election in Alaska to be held under a new election process provided for in [[2020 Alaska Measure 2|Ballot Measure 2]]. All candidates ran in a [[top-four primary#Alaska|nonpartisan blanket top-four primary]] on August 16, 2022, and the top four candidates advanced to the general election, where voters utilized [[instant-runoff voting|ranked-choice voting]].{{Cite news |first=Andrew |last=Kitchenman |date=November 18, 2020 |title=Alaska will have a new election system: Voters pass Ballot Measure 2 |url=https://www.ktoo.org/2020/11/17/alaska-will-have-a-new-election-system-voters-pass-ballot-measure-2/ |access-date=November 18, 2020 |work=[[KTOO (FM)]] |language=en-US |archive-date=November 18, 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201118052421/https://www.ktoo.org/2020/11/17/alaska-will-have-a-new-election-system-voters-pass-ballot-measure-2/ |url-status=live}}{{Cite web|title=Alaska Division of Elections, Primary Election Info|url=https://www.elections.alaska.gov/Core/primaryelectioninformation.php|access-date=December 10, 2021|archive-date=May 4, 2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220504030110/https://www.elections.alaska.gov/Core/primaryelectioninformation.php|url-status=live}} Murkowski had been a vocal critic of [[Donald Trump]] during his presidency and opposed several of his initiatives. Murkowski was one of seven Republican senators who voted to convict Trump in his [[Second impeachment trial of Donald Trump|second impeachment trial]] in 2021, and was the only one up for re-election in 2022. On March 16, 2021, the [[Alaska Republican Party]] voted to censure Murkowski and announced that it would recruit a Republican challenger in the 2022 election cycle.
